definition: Direct evidence directly links a person to a crime; it demonstrates "the ultimate fact to be proved" (see: Oliver v. State). U.S. vs Shawntell Curry also holds that “direct evidence is the testimony of a person who claims to have personal knowledge of the commission of the crime which has been charged, such as an eyewitness”. It is also written in Georgia Code, Title 24 – Evidence Charter 1 that, “Direct evidence” means evidence which immediately points to the question at issue.” Compare to circumstantial evidence. diplomatic immunity / direct evidence Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026
